q: A railway public sector undertaking provides consultancy services for transport and other infrastructure projects in India and abroad. It is:

options.A: IRCON International Limited
options.B: Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation
options.D: RITES Limited

e: RITES Limited is the Railways PSU specialising in transport and infrastructure consultancy, including projects in India and abroad, unlike IRCON (construction), IRCTC (catering and tourism) or RVNL (project execution).

q: Liabilities incurred on works but not yet paid or discharged are watched through the Liability Register, which is maintained in the:

options.A: Accounts office
options.B: Office of the contractor executing the work
options.D: Office of the Station Master

e: The Liability Register, kept in the Accounts office, records liabilities incurred on works but not yet paid or discharged, so that commitments are watched and provided for before payment.

q: At the abutments of a bridge, wing walls are provided primarily in order to:

options.A: Carry the track over the bridge
options.B: Retain the approach embankment and guide the stream towards the waterway of the bridge
options.C: Support the bearings of the girders
options.D: Provide a footpath for the use of the patrolmen

e: Wing walls at bridge abutments retain the approach embankment and guide the stream into the bridge waterway, preventing erosion and directing flow; girder bearings rest on the abutments themselves.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Departmental (centage) charges are added to the estimates of the Railways' own works in the same manner as for deposit works.
2. On a work executed by the Railways for an outside body, departmental charges are recovered to cover the cost of the establishment and tools and plant employed in executing and supervising it.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct. Departmental charges are recovered on works done for outside bodies to cover establishment and tools and plant costs; they are not added to the Railways own works in the same manner.

q: Approaching a level crossing, the driver of a train is required to sound the whistle from the point marked by the:

options.A: Speed restriction board
options.B: Fouling mark board
options.D: Gradient post

e: The W/L board is the Whistle Level-crossing board. Fixed before a level crossing, it marks the point from which the driver must sound the whistle to warn road users of the approaching train.

q: Under a 'labour contract' for the execution of a work on the Railways, the materials for the work are supplied by the Railways and the contractor is engaged only for:

options.A: Supervising the work of departmental labour
options.B: Transporting the materials to the site
options.C: Providing the labour for the work
options.D: Maintaining the completed work for one year

e: In a labour contract the Railways supply the materials and the contractor supplies only the labour for execution, as distinct from a full works contract where the contractor provides both labour and materials.

q: In the course of a financial year, a division furnishes estimates of the expenditure likely to be incurred by the year-end, assessed from the progress of expenditure so far. These are known as:

options.A: Out-turn estimates
options.B: Budget estimates for the next year
options.D: Final Modification estimates

e: Out-turn estimates show the expenditure likely to be incurred by the year-end, judged from the progress of expenditure so far in the year; they feed the revised and final stages of the budget.

q: The classification of railway transactions and the rules for the maintenance of accounts are contained in:

options.A: Volume I of the Indian Railway Financial Code
options.B: The Indian Railway Establishment Code
options.C: Volume II of the Indian Railway Financial Code, containing the Accounts Code
options.D: The Indian Railways Stores Code

e: Volume II of the Indian Railway Financial Code is the Accounts Code. It contains the classification of transactions and the rules for maintenance of railway accounts; Volume I deals with financial rules generally.

q: Before a proposed new railway line is taken up for detailed investigation, a survey is carried out to judge its technical feasibility and its economic and financial viability. This survey is the:

options.A: Final location survey
options.B: Reconnaissance survey of the district
options.D: Techno-economic survey

e: A techno-economic survey precedes detailed investigation of a new line. It examines technical feasibility together with economic and financial viability, including the expected return on the investment.

q: Stores issued from a depot for use on a work are debited to the work at their book value plus an addition covering the cost of procurement, inspection, storage and handling. This addition is known as:

options.A: Departmental charges
options.B: Percentage (overhead) charges on stores
options.D: Agency charges

e: Stores issued to a work are charged at book value plus percentage overhead charges on stores, which recover the cost of procurement, inspection, storage and handling incurred by the stores organisation.

q: A new class of rolling stock is proposed to be introduced on a section. The ceiling speed at which it may be allowed to run is governed by the 'speed certificate' issued by:

options.A: The Commissioner of Railway Safety
options.B: The Railway Board
options.D: The Divisional Railway Manager

e: RDSO, the Railways research and standards body, issues the speed certificate that fixes the maximum permissible speed for new or modified rolling stock based on its design and trial results.

q: The Konkan Railway line was constructed and is operated by a corporation jointly promoted by the Indian Railways together with the States of:

options.A: Maharashtra alone
options.B: Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala
options.D: Goa alone

e: The Konkan Railway was built and is operated by Konkan Railway Corporation, promoted by Indian Railways jointly with Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka and Kerala, the states through which the line passes.

q: For a newly constructed railway line, the liability to pay dividend on its capital-at-charge remains deferred, as a deferred dividend liability, during:

options.A: The period of construction only
options.B: The first three years after the line is opened to traffic
options.C: The first ten years after the line is opened to traffic
options.D: The period of construction and the first five years after the line is opened to traffic

e: For a new line, dividend on capital-at-charge is treated as a deferred dividend liability during construction and for the first five years after opening to traffic, the moratorium period allowed for the line to develop traffic.

q: In railway works accounts, the fund or head of account to which the cost of a work is chargeable, such as Capital, Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund or Revenue, is known as the work's:

options.A: Allocation
options.B: Sanction
options.D: Throw-forward

e: Allocation denotes the fund or head to which a work cost is chargeable, such as Capital, DRF, Development Fund or Revenue. Expenditure must follow the sanctioned allocation in the Works Register and accounts.

q: An allotment for a work is found to be surplus to the expenditure likely to be incurred on it during the financial year. The correct treatment of the surplus allotment is to:

options.A: Spend it quickly on any available work before the close of the year
options.B: Carry it forward automatically to the next year
options.C: Surrender it promptly, so that the funds can be allotted for other purposes
options.D: Transfer it to the staff welfare fund

e: Surplus allotment must be surrendered promptly under budget rules, so the funds can be re-allotted to other works. Allotments lapse at year-end and cannot be diverted or carried forward by the division itself.

q: A supplier whose goods, services or works have local content of less than 20 per cent is classified under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order as a:

options.A: Class-I local supplier
options.B: Class-II local supplier
options.D: Non-local supplier

e: Under the Public Procurement Preference to Make in India Order, local content of 50 percent or more is Class-I and 20 to 50 percent is Class-II; below 20 percent the supplier is a non-local supplier.

q: At the very initial stage of a proposal for a private siding, the applicant firm is required to deposit the:

options.A: Cost of constructing the serving station
options.B: Charges for the survey of the siding and the preparation of its plans and estimate
options.C: Cost of the junction arrangements on the main line
options.D: Half of the cost of the land for the siding

e: At the initial stage of a private siding proposal, the applicant deposits the survey charges covering the survey and preparation of plans and estimate, before the siding scheme is examined and sanctioned.

q: The processing of a work for sanction follows the sequence:

options.A: Expenditure sanction, then administrative approval, then technical sanction
options.B: Technical sanction, then expenditure sanction, then administrative approval
options.C: Administrative approval, then preparation of the detailed estimate and its technical sanction, then expenditure sanction
options.D: Administrative approval, then expenditure sanction, then preparation of the detailed estimate

e: The sequence is administrative approval first, then preparation of the detailed estimate and its technical sanction, and finally expenditure sanction, which alone authorises expenditure to be incurred.

q: The detailed estimate of a work receives its technical sanction from:

options.A: The Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer
options.B: The Accounts Officer of the division
options.D: The competent engineering authority

e: Technical sanction to a detailed estimate is accorded by the competent engineering authority, which certifies the design and estimate as technically sound; finance concurrence is separate from technical sanction.

q: For computing the anticipated rate of return of a railway project, the 'net gain' is arrived at by deducting from the anticipated gross earnings the:

options.A: Working expenses, including maintenance and the provision for depreciation
options.B: Dividend payable on the capital-at-charge only
options.C: Cost of the land required for the project only
options.D: Cost of the surveys and investigations only

e: Net gain for the rate of return is gross earnings minus working expenses, including maintenance and depreciation provision. Comparing this net gain with capital-at-charge gives the anticipated return.

q: Way-leave charges recovered from parties for the use of railway land are accounted for as:

options.A: Capital receipts of the Railways
options.B: Credits to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Earnings (revenue receipts) of the Railways

e: Way-leave charges for use of railway land are revenue receipts and are credited to earnings, not to Capital or a fund, because they are a recurring income from an existing asset.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On acquisition of land for a project, the entries in the revenue records are changed so that the land stands recorded in the name of the Railways.
2. Railway land which a zonal railway finds surplus to its needs can be sold by that railway under its own powers.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. Acquired land is mutated in revenue records in the Railways name, but a zonal railway cannot sell surplus railway land on its own authority; disposal needs higher sanction.

q: The register maintained in the Accounts office to watch that the expenditure on works and repairs is borne by the correct fund or head, such as Capital, Depreciation Reserve Fund, Development Fund or Revenue, is the:

options.A: Register of Sanctions
options.B: Works Register
options.D: Revenue Allocation Register

e: The Revenue Allocation Register in Accounts watches that works and repairs expenditure is borne by the correct fund or head - Capital, DRF, Development Fund or Revenue - as per the allocation rules.

q: A contract in which three parties are involved — the creditor, the principal debtor and the surety — as distinct from a contract of indemnity which involves only two parties, is a contract of:

options.A: Agency
options.B: Bailment
options.D: Pledge

e: A contract of guarantee under the Indian Contract Act involves three parties - creditor, principal debtor and surety - whereas a contract of indemnity involves only two parties.

q: In the law of contract, a Notice Inviting Tender issued by the Railways for a work amounts to:

options.A: An offer
options.B: An invitation to offer
options.D: A concluded agreement

e: A Notice Inviting Tender is only an invitation to offer under contract law. The tender submitted is the offer, and a contract arises only when the Railways accept it and communicate acceptance.

q: A suit for compensation for breach of a contract must be filed within the period of limitation of:

options.A: One year
options.B: Five years
options.D: Three years

e: Under the Limitation Act, the period for a suit for compensation for breach of contract is three years from the breach or, if successive, from the breach complained of.

q: Major projects of a zonal railway, such as new lines, gauge conversion and doubling, are executed by its construction organisation, which works under the overall control of the:

options.A: Chief Administrative Officer (Construction)
options.B: Divisional Railway Manager
options.D: Financial Adviser and Chief Accounts Officer

e: Major construction works like new lines, gauge conversion and doubling are executed by the construction organisation headed by the Chief Administrative Officer (Construction) of the zonal railway.

q: A division proposes an improvement work which is operationally necessary, but its anticipated return falls short of the test of financial remunerativeness. Such a work is ordinarily financed from:

options.A: The Development Fund
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Revenue (working expenses)

e: The Development Fund finances operationally necessary improvement works that are not financially remunerative, such as passenger amenity and operational improvements failing the normal return test.

q: For the acquisition of land for a 'special railway project' under the Railways Act, 1989, the acquisition proceedings are carried out by:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal railway
options.B: The Commissioner of Railway Safety
options.D: An officer notified by the Central Government, ordinarily a revenue officer such as the District Collector

e: For a special railway project under the Railways Act, 1989, land acquisition is done by the competent authority notified by the Central Government, ordinarily a revenue officer like the District Collector.

q: A road under-bridge below a running track is commonly built without interrupting train traffic by the technique of:

options.A: Box pushing, in which pre-cast RCC boxes are jacked into the embankment under the track
options.B: Open excavation after closing the line to traffic for several weeks
options.D: Dismantling the track and relaying it after construction

e: Box pushing builds a road under-bridge without interrupting traffic: pre-cast RCC boxes are jacked through the embankment under the running track, avoiding open excavation and line blocks.

q: On a delayed work, liquidated damages go on being levied week after week and the contractor contends that they can keep accumulating without any ceiling. Under the General Conditions of Contract, the total liquidated damages leviable under a works contract cannot exceed:

options.A: 5% of the contract value
options.B: 10% of the contract value
options.D: 25% of the contract value

e: Under the GCC for works, liquidated damages for delay are levied at the prescribed rate but the total is capped at 10 percent of the contract value, so LD cannot accumulate without a ceiling.

q: A contractor brings durable materials to the site for incorporation in the work and applies for a secured advance against them. The secured advance payable against such materials shall not ordinarily exceed:

options.A: 75% of the value of the materials
options.B: 50% of the value of the materials
options.C: 90% of the value of the materials
options.D: 100% of the value of the materials

e: A secured advance against durable materials brought to site for incorporation in the work is limited ordinarily to 75 percent of the value of those materials, assessed by the Engineer, under the GCC.

q:
Consider the following statements about mobilisation advance in a works contract:
1. It is ordinarily limited to 10% of the contract value.
2. It is interest-bearing, the interest being recovered along with the advance from the contractor's bills.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Mobilisation advance is ordinarily up to 10 percent of contract value and is interest-bearing, the advance and interest being recovered from the contractors on-account bills.

q: For a very large works tender, a tenderer objects that the earnest money demanded works out to far more than the prescribed ceiling. The Earnest Money Deposit required from tenderers in works tenders is subject to a maximum (cap) of:

options.A: Rs 10 lakh
options.B: Rs 25 lakh
options.D: Rs 50 lakh

e: Under GCC April 2022 (Clause 5, Bid Security), for a work estimated above Rs 1 crore the bid security is Rs 2 lakh plus 0.5 percent of the excess beyond Rs 1 crore, subject to a maximum of Rs 1 crore - so the earnest money that can be demanded from tenderers is capped at Rs 1 crore.

q: The successful tenderer neither furnishes the Performance Guarantee/Security Deposit within the period stipulated after the issue of the Letter of Acceptance nor seeks any extension. In such a case, the Railways may:

options.A: Waive the requirement of the guarantee altogether
options.B: Cancel the acceptance of the tender and forfeit the Earnest Money Deposit
options.C: Furnish the guarantee amount on behalf of the contractor
options.D: Extend the period indefinitely without any condition

e: If the successful tenderer fails to furnish the Performance Guarantee or Security Deposit in time and seeks no extension, the Railways may cancel the acceptance and forfeit the Earnest Money Deposit under the GCC.

q: In a works tender invited under the two-packet system, the technical packet of a tenderer is evaluated and found not to meet the eligibility conditions of the tender. The correct treatment of his financial packet is that:

options.A: It is not opened, since the financial packets of only those tenderers whose technical/eligibility packets are found acceptable are opened
options.B: It is opened first and the technical packet is examined later
options.C: It is opened along with all other financial packets simultaneously
options.D: It is opened after the Letter of Acceptance is issued to another tenderer

e: In the two-packet system only the technical packet is opened and evaluated first. Financial packets of tenderers failing eligibility are not opened; only those found technically acceptable proceed to financial opening.

q:
Consider the following statements about negotiations on a works tender:
1. If the lowest (L1) tenderer does not accept the counter-offer made to him, negotiations may then be held with the next higher (L2) tenderer.
2. Where negotiations become unavoidable, they are held only with the lowest (L1) tenderer; if they fail to bring the rates to a reasonable level, the tenders may be rejected and fresh tenders invited.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct. Negotiations, where unavoidable, are held only with the L1 tenderer; if they fail to secure reasonable rates, tenders may be rejected and fresh tenders invited - negotiation does not move to L2.

q: During execution, the scope and quantities of a contract are changed so extensively that the work finally executed bears little resemblance to the work originally contracted for. A change so large that it changes the entire character of the contract is called:

options.A: Variation
options.B: Deviation
options.D: Extra item

e: A change so extensive that the executed work bears little resemblance to the original contract changes its entire character and is called vitiation of the contract, distinct from ordinary variation or deviation.

q: An executive proposes to carry out a major change in the scope and design of a sanctioned work first and obtain sanction for the change after the modified work is completed. In respect of a material modification of a sanctioned work, the correct requirement is:

options.A: Sanction of the contractor executing the work
options.B: Sanction only after the whole work is completed
options.C: Approval of the Railway Board in every case, however small the modification
options.D: Prior sanction of the competent authority, with finance concurrence, before the modified portion of the work is executed

e: A material modification of a sanctioned work needs prior sanction of the competent authority with finance concurrence before the modified portion is executed; post-facto sanction after completion is not the rule.

q: During a periodic check, a difference is noticed between the expenditure shown against a work in the executive office register and the figure booked for the same work in the accounts office. Such differences come to light because the figures entered in the Works Register are:

options.A: Compared only with the contractor's own books of account
options.B: Periodically reconciled with the figures booked in the accounts office, so that differences are noticed and set right
options.C: Examined for the first time only during audit inspection
options.D: Accepted as correct without any comparison with the accounts figures

e: Works Register figures in the executive office are periodically reconciled with figures booked in the Accounts office, so differences between the two records are noticed and set right promptly.

q: On completion of a work, serviceable materials issued for it remain surplus and are returned by the executive to the stores depot. In the accounts of the work, such returned materials are:

options.A: Taken back into stock, and the work is given credit for their value
options.B: Treated as scrap in all cases
options.D: Charged to the contractor at penal rates in all cases

e: Serviceable surplus materials returned to stores are taken back into stock and the work is credited with their value, reducing the works cost; they are not written off or treated automatically as scrap.

q: An accounts scrutiny notes a debit balance standing under Miscellaneous Works Advances in connection with a work. Such a debit balance represents:

options.A: Compensation paid by the Railways to contractors for delay in completion of works
options.B: The profit earned by the Railways on the work
options.C: Amounts outstanding for recovery or adjustment in connection with works
options.D: Departmental charges recovered on deposit works

e: A debit balance under Miscellaneous Works Advances represents amounts spent in connection with works that are outstanding for recovery or adjustment, for example recoverable dues pending clearance.

q: Midway through a deposit work, it becomes clear that its cost will exceed the amount deposited by the outside body. The correct course is that:

options.A: The excess is automatically borne by the Railways
options.B: The contractor executing the work is asked to bear the excess
options.C: The excess is adjusted against the departmental charges of another work
options.D: The party should be called upon to deposit the additional amount required, and expenditure beyond the deposit should not be incurred in anticipation of it

e: On a deposit work, expenditure must stay within the deposit. If cost will exceed it, the party must be called upon to deposit the extra amount first; excess must not be incurred in anticipation of the deposit.

q: The departmental charges recovered from outside parties on deposit works are accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting them to the earnings (revenue receipts) of the Railways
options.B: Retaining them with the executing division as its own funds
options.C: Depositing them in the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: Refunding them to the parties on completion of the works

e: Departmental charges recovered on deposit works are credited to the earnings of the Railways, since they reimburse establishment and supervision costs and form a revenue receipt.

q: The departmental/agency charges levied on works are also commonly known as centage charges because:

options.A: They are recovered in cash at the cash office
options.B: They are charged only on works costing more than one crore
options.C: They are levied as a percentage of the cost of the work
options.D: They are adjusted through the Contractor's Ledger

e: Departmental or agency charges are called centage charges simply because they are levied as a percentage of the cost of the work, centage meaning a rate per cent.

q: In a works contract with a price variation clause, the price indices for the relevant components fall during execution and the contractor argues that the adjustment can only ever operate in his favour. Under the price variation clause, the adjustment operates:

options.A: Only in favour of the contractor
options.B: Only in favour of the Railways
options.C: Both ways — the amount payable increases when the indices rise and decreases when the indices fall
options.D: Only in contracts executed departmentally

e: A price variation clause works both ways: payment rises when the prescribed indices rise and falls when they fall. It is a neutral adjustment for price changes, not a one-sided benefit to the contractor.

q:
Consider the following statements about price variation in a works contract:
1. Price variation is payable in every works contract, whether or not a price variation clause is included in the contract.
2. Price variation is payable only where the contract expressly provides a price variation clause.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct. Price variation is payable only if the contract expressly contains a price variation clause; without such a clause no escalation or de-escalation claim arises.

q: A work is delayed entirely for reasons attributable to the contractor and extension of time is granted to him. As provided in the contract conditions, the price variation payable in respect of the extended period is generally:

options.A: Computed with the price indices of the extended period in all cases
options.B: Paid at double the normal rate
options.D: Restricted by freezing the indices at those prevailing on the original stipulated date of completion

e: Where delay is attributable to the contractor, price variation for the extended period is restricted by freezing indices at those prevailing on the original stipulated completion date, so delay earns no extra escalation.

q: An extra item, for which no directly applicable rate exists in the contract, has to be paid for. The rate payable for such an extra item is ordinarily derived:

options.A: From the rate of a similar item in the contract itself and, failing that, from the schedule of rates adjusted by the tenderer's overall percentage above or below the schedule
options.B: Purely at the discretion of the contractor
options.C: At twice the schedule rate for the item
options.D: From the rates accepted in another railway's contract

e: An extra item rate is derived first from a similar contract item and, failing that, from the schedule of rates adjusted by the tenderers overall percentage above or below the schedule, per the GCC method.

q: On a work, the quantity of an item actually executed goes well beyond the deviation limit laid down in the contract, and the contractor claims the contract rate for the entire quantity as a matter of right. The correct position is that:

options.A: The excess quantity is paid for at twice the contract rate
options.B: The rate for the quantity executed in excess of the deviation limit is settled in accordance with the provisions of the contract, and the contract rate does not automatically apply to it
options.D: The contractor may refuse to execute the excess quantity in all cases

e: Beyond the deviation limit in the contract, the contract rate does not automatically apply to the excess quantity; the rate for that excess is settled under the specific deviation provisions of the contract.

q:
On a building work, the Engineer orders an altogether new item that finds no place in the original contract, and on another portion he directs that a different item be executed in lieu of an item originally provided. Consider the following statements about these two directions:
1. The altogether new item so ordered is an extra item, being additional to the items provided in the original contract.
2. The item executed in lieu of the item originally provided is a substituted item.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. An altogether new item not in the original contract is an extra item, while an item executed in place of an item originally provided is a substituted item, under GCC definitions.

q: An official finds that a figure entered by him in the Measurement Book is wrong. The entry is required to be corrected by:

options.A: Erasing the original entry and rewriting it
options.B: Overwriting the correct figures over the original entry
options.C: Tearing out the page containing the entry
options.D: Striking out the entry, with the correction attested by the initials and date of the official making it

e: A wrong Measurement Book entry is corrected by striking it out so the original remains legible, writing the correction and attesting it with the initials and date of the official making the correction.

q: The Engineer orders the opening up of work already executed and covered up, and on inspection the work is found to conform to the contract. The cost of such opening up, testing and reinstatement is borne by:

options.A: The Railways
options.B: The contractor in all cases
options.D: The contractor and the Railways in equal shares

e: If work ordered to be opened up for inspection is found to conform to the contract, the Railways bear the cost of opening, testing and reinstatement; the contractor bears it only if the work is found defective.

q: Measurements of work done recorded in the Measurement Book by an official are required to be:

options.A: Accepted without any check in all cases
options.B: Test-checked by his superior officer to the extent prescribed
options.D: Checked only after the final bill is paid

e: Measurements recorded in the Measurement Book must be test-checked by the superior officer to the extent prescribed, ensuring accuracy before bills based on those measurements are passed for payment.

q: A contractor fails to submit his final bill within the period stipulated in the contract. In that event:

options.A: No final bill can ever be prepared for the work
options.B: The work is treated as abandoned
options.C: The final bill is prepared by the Engineer on the basis of the measurements recorded, and it is binding on the contractor
options.D: The earnest money deposits of all the tenderers are forfeited

e: If the contractor fails to submit his final bill in the stipulated period, the Engineer prepares the final bill from the recorded measurements, and that bill is binding on the contractor under the GCC.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. On-account (running) payments made to a contractor are in the nature of advance payments, adjustable against the final settlement of the contract.
2. An overpayment made to a contractor in an on-account bill, if detected later, cannot be recovered from him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. On-account payments are advances adjustable at final settlement, and any overpayment detected later is recoverable from the contractor from sums due to him.

q: At the time of an on-account bill, an item of work under the contract is only partly complete. Payment for such an item is made:

options.A: At the full contract rate in all cases
options.B: Only after the whole contract is completed
options.C: At the rate quoted by the next higher tenderer
options.D: At a part rate assessed by the Engineer with reference to the proportion of the item completed

e: For a partly completed item in an on-account bill, payment is made at a part rate assessed by the Engineer in proportion to the work actually done on that item, not at the full contract rate.

q: A work of small value is completed in one single operation and no running payments are called for. Payment to the contractor for such a work may be made through:

options.A: A secured advance bill
options.B: A first and final bill
options.D: A percentage-rate bill

e: A small work completed in one operation, needing no running payments, is paid through a first and final bill, which serves as both the first and the closing bill for the work.

q: The electronic Measurement Book (e-MB) for works contracts, on which contractors also submit their bills online against works contracts, is maintained on:

options.A: IREPS
options.B: FOIS
options.C: IRWCMS (Indian Railways Works Contract Management System)
options.D: IPAS

e: The electronic Measurement Book and online contractor billing for works contracts are maintained on IRWCMS, the Indian Railways Works Contract Management System, replacing the manual MB process.

q: Before a contractor's on-account or final bill is prepared, an Abstract of Measurements is prepared in order to:

options.A: Summarise, item-wise, the quantities of work measured in the Measurement Book on which the bill is based
options.B: Record the hindrances met during the execution of the work
options.C: Tabulate the rates quoted by all the tenderers
options.D: Work out the departmental charges of the work

e: The Abstract of Measurements summarises item-wise the quantities measured in the Measurement Book on which a contractors bill is based, linking each billed quantity to its MB entries.

q: Before a works contract is determined on account of the contractor's default, an initial notice is served calling upon him to remedy the default. After that initial notice, the final notice served on the contractor before determination is of:

options.A: 7 days
options.B: 24 hours
options.D: 48 hours

e: Under GCC termination procedure, a 7-day notice to remedy default is followed by a final notice of 48 hours before the contract is determined for the contractors default.

q: A contractor owes the Railways amounts under one works contract, while payments are becoming due to him under another contract with the Railway. Amounts found due from a contractor under a contract may be recovered:

options.A: Only from the security deposit of that very contract
options.B: From any sums due or becoming due to the contractor under that contract or any other contract with the Railway
options.C: Only after obtaining a decree of a competent court
options.D: From the earnest money deposits of unsuccessful tenderers

e: Sums due from a contractor may be recovered from any amounts due or becoming due to him under the same contract or any other contract with the Railway, under the GCC recovery clause.

q: A dispute arises on a matter which the General Conditions of Contract treat as an 'excepted matter', and the contractor demands that it be referred to arbitration. In respect of such excepted matters:

options.A: The decision of the contractor is final
options.B: The decision of the tender committee is final
options.C: The decision of the Engineer is final and binding on the parties, and the matter cannot be referred to arbitration
options.D: The dispute must necessarily be referred to arbitration

e: Excepted matters are decided by the Engineer, whose decision is final and binding and cannot be referred to arbitration; the arbitration clause of the GCC expressly excludes such matters.

q: An arbitral award made under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 in a works dispute is not set aside by any court. Such an award is:

options.A: Enforceable in the same manner as a decree of a court
options.B: Merely advisory in nature
options.C: Binding only if the contractor agrees to it
options.D: Valid only for one year from the date of the award

e: Under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, an arbitral award that is not set aside is enforceable in the same manner as a decree of a court, through execution proceedings.

q: A works contract is terminated for the contractor's default and the contractor then seeks settlement of disputes arising out of that very contract. The arbitration clause contained in the contract, in such a situation:

options.A: Comes to an end automatically as soon as the contract is terminated
options.B: Can be invoked only while the work is still in progress
options.C: Is replaced by the decision of the Engineer once the contract is terminated
options.D: Continues to operate for the settlement of disputes arising out of the contract, even after the contract has been terminated

e: The arbitration clause is separable from the main contract and survives its termination, so disputes arising out of a terminated contract can still be settled under that clause.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Events such as war, flood, earthquake or epidemic, which are beyond the control of the parties and prevent the performance of the contract, are treated as force majeure events, and on their occurrence the period of completion is suitably extended with neither party liable for damages for the delay so caused.
2. A contract becomes void under the doctrine of frustration merely because the contractor finds the work unprofitable to execute.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct. War, flood, earthquake or epidemic are force majeure events justifying extension without damages; mere unprofitability is not frustration and does not void a contract.

q:
Consider the following statements about subletting of a works contract:
1. Once a portion of the work is sublet with the consent of the Railways, the Railways can proceed only against the sub-contractor for any defect in that portion.
2. Even where the Railway consents to the subletting of a portion of a work, the contractor remains fully responsible to the Railways for the whole work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 2 is correct. Even with the Railways consent to subletting part of a work, the original contractor remains fully responsible to the Railways for the whole work, including the sublet portion.

q: A supplier suggests that a zonal railway should invite its works tenders through the Government e-Marketplace. The correct position is that:

options.A: Works contracts of the Railways are procured through GeM in all cases
options.B: Works tenders are invited through GeM only for works above Rs 50 lakh
options.C: Works contracts are not invited through GeM; works tenders are invited through the IREPS e-tendering system, GeM being used for online procurement of goods and services
options.D: Works tenders are purchased like stores items through the stores portal

e: Works contracts are not procured through GeM, which covers goods and services. Railway works tenders are invited through the IREPS e-tendering system under the works GCC.

q: In e-tendering through IREPS for works, offers for a tender can be submitted:

options.A: In sealed covers at the divisional office as an alternative to online submission
options.B: By depositing the earnest money in cash at the cash office in all cases
options.C: Manually, in the contractor's office, after online registration
options.D: Only online through the portal, the tenderer registering on IREPS and submitting the bid using a valid digital signature certificate; manual or physical offers are not considered

e: In IREPS e-tendering, bids are submitted only online by a tenderer registered on the portal using a valid digital signature certificate; manual or physical offers are not entertained.

q: An estimator complains that the USSOR rates issued some years ago no longer reflect the present-day cost of labour and materials. These schedule rates are brought up to date by:

options.A: Revising them with reference to cost indices that reflect changes in the prices of labour and materials
options.B: Substituting, for each item, the lowest rate quoted in recent tenders
options.C: Leaving the printed rates untouched and adjusting only the quantities in estimates
options.D: Rewriting the schedule afresh only when a new Works Programme is prepared

e: USSOR schedule rates are updated by applying cost indices reflecting changes in labour and material prices, keeping the unified standard schedule aligned with present-day costs.

q: A sanctioned work provides for doubling of an existing single-line section to augment line capacity. In the Works Programme, doubling works are classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 11
options.B: Plan Head 31
options.D: Plan Head 21

e: In the Works Programme, doubling of a single line to augment capacity is classified under Plan Head 15, which covers doubling works, distinct from new lines, track renewals and other plan heads.

q: A road under-bridge is taken up in lieu of a level crossing as a road safety work. Works relating to road over-bridges and road under-bridges taken up for road safety are classified under:

options.A: Plan Head 29 — Road Safety Works (Level Crossings)
options.B: Plan Head 16 — Traffic Facilities
options.D: Plan Head 30 — Road Safety Works (ROB/RUB)

e: Road over-bridges and road under-bridges taken up in lieu of level crossings for road safety are classified under Plan Head 30, Road Safety Works (ROB/RUB); Plan Head 29 covers level crossing works.

q: A work provides for construction of a road over-bridge in place of a level crossing as a safety measure at level crossings. Works of this nature are financed mainly from:

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund
options.D: The Capital Fund

e: Road over and under-bridges in lieu of level crossings are financed mainly from the Railway Safety Fund, the fund created for works that eliminate level crossing accidents.

q: An existing asset is renewed and, at the same time, improved to a higher standard. The cost of such a work is:

options.A: Charged wholly to Capital in all cases
options.B: Charged wholly to Revenue
options.C: Apportioned, the cost of like-for-like renewal being charged to the renewal head (such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund) and the additional cost of the improvement to the appropriate capital head
options.D: Recovered from the contractor executing the renewal

e: For renewal with improvement, cost is apportioned: like-for-like renewal is charged to the renewal source such as DRF, and only the extra cost of improvement goes to Capital or the appropriate capital head.

q: For a major works contract, the contractor takes out Contractor's All Risks (CAR) insurance to cover the work against loss or damage during execution. The insurance policies taken out by the contractor under the General Conditions of Contract are required to be in the joint names of:

options.A: The contractor and his bank
options.B: The contractor and the Engineer personally
options.D: The Railways and the contractor

e: Contractors All Risks and other policies taken under the GCC must be in the joint names of the Railways and the contractor, so both interests in the work are protected by the insurance.

q: A zonal railway finds a station improvement work listed in the approved Works Programme and proposes to start it straightaway, even though no estimate for it has yet been sanctioned. The correct position is that:

options.A: Listing in the programme itself sanctions the estimate
options.B: Listing only makes the work part of the approved programme; expenditure can be incurred only after its estimate is sanctioned by the competent authority
options.C: The work may start if the tender committee so recommends
options.D: Funds for a listed work can be drawn without any estimate

e: Inclusion in the approved Works Programme only lists a work in the programme. No expenditure can be incurred until its estimate is sanctioned by the competent authority.

q: A bridge approach is washed away in floods and immediate restoration is essential for safe train running, though the work does not figure in the sanctioned Works Programme. Such a work may be taken up out of turn when:

options.A: It is of an urgent nature, such as an urgent safety or restoration work, and is sanctioned by the competent authority within its powers
options.B: The contractor working in the section offers to execute it
options.C: The division happens to have spare labour available
options.D: The work happens to be a deposit work

e: A work outside the sanctioned programme may be taken up out of turn only if it is urgent, such as urgent safety or flood restoration work, and is sanctioned by the competent authority within its powers.

q: Against a large sanctioned work, the budget for the year carries only a nominal allotment, the bulk of the money being expected in later years as the work progresses. Such a nominal allotment is known as a:

options.A: Supplementary provision
options.B: Re-appropriation
options.D: Lapsed provision

e: A token provision is a nominal budget allotment for a large sanctioned work in a year, signalling the work is on the programme while the bulk of funds is expected in later years.

q: Before the annual Works Programme is finalised, each zonal railway sends up a preliminary list of works it proposes for inclusion. This preliminary list submitted to the Railway Board for selection of works is called the:

options.A: List of Approved Works
options.B: Completion programme
options.D: Preliminary Works Programme

e: The Preliminary Works Programme is the preliminary list of proposed works sent by each zonal railway to the Railway Board, from which works are selected for the final Works Programme.

q: During execution of a sanctioned work, the executive decides to change its scope in a way that materially alters the sanctioned provisions. Before the changed portion is executed, the executive must obtain:

options.A: Prior sanction of the competent authority for the material modification, with finance concurrence
options.B: Only the verbal approval of the contractor
options.C: Sanction after the whole work has been completed
options.D: Approval of the Railway Board in every case, however small the change

e: A material modification altering the sanctioned scope of a work needs prior sanction of the competent authority with finance concurrence before the changed portion is executed, not after completion.

q: A proposal for an entirely new work is put up for approval in principle before any detailed estimate is prepared. Such administrative approval is normally accorded on the basis of:

options.A: The final bill of a similar work executed earlier
options.B: The accepted tender for the work
options.C: An abstract estimate accompanied by a report explaining the necessity and justification of the work
options.D: The completion estimate of the work

e: Administrative approval is accorded in principle on an abstract estimate with a report explaining the necessity and justification of the work, before any detailed estimate is prepared.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Technical sanction relates to the technical soundness of the design and of the detailed estimate of a work.
2. Expenditure sanction is the authority of the competent authority permitting expenditure to be incurred on a work.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Technical sanction certifies the technical soundness of the design and detailed estimate, while expenditure sanction is the competent authoritys permission to incur the expenditure.

q: Midway through a work, rising prices and other causes make it clear that the final cost will materially exceed the amount originally sanctioned. The estimate that must then be prepared is a:

options.A: Supplementary estimate
options.B: Abstract estimate
options.D: Revised estimate

e: When cost in progress will materially exceed the sanctioned amount, a revised estimate is prepared and sanctioned to cover the anticipated final cost of the work as a whole.

q: While a sanctioned work is in progress, certain additions and alterations not covered by the original sanction are found necessary. These are provided for through a:

options.A: Supplementary estimate
options.B: Token estimate
options.D: Rough cost estimate

e: Additions and alterations found necessary during execution, beyond the original sanction, are provided for by a supplementary estimate sanctioned in addition to the original estimate.

q: A work is in its final stages and the executive wants to arrive at its final cost as actually executed and obtain sanction for it where necessary. The document prepared at this stage is the:

options.A: Abstract estimate
options.B: Detailed estimate
options.D: Preliminary estimate

e: A completion estimate is prepared at the final stage to record the actual final cost of the work as executed and to obtain sanction for any excess over the sanctioned estimate where required.

q: A contract for cleaning and housekeeping services is sought to be governed by the same conditions as a contract for construction of a building. This is incorrect because:

options.A: Services contracts need no written conditions at all
options.B: Separate General Conditions of Contract exist for Works contracts and for Services contracts
options.C: A single common GCC governs both works and services contracts
options.D: Services are always executed departmentally

e: Separate General Conditions of Contract exist for works and for services, because construction works and service contracts differ in nature; the works GCC does not govern a cleaning or housekeeping service.

q: Two documents forming part of the same contract give conflicting directions on a point, and the contractor insists on following the one that suits him. The conflict is to be resolved according to:

options.A: The preference of the contractor
options.B: The date of the oldest document
options.C: The discretion of the sectional staff
options.D: The order of precedence of the documents laid down in the contract conditions

e: Conflicts between contract documents are resolved by the order of precedence laid down in the contract conditions, not by the contractors preference or by the date of a document.

q: A contractor, without asking the Railway, hands over a portion of his work to another firm to execute. Under the General Conditions of Contract, this is impermissible because a contractor:

options.A: Cannot sublet or assign the work, or any part of it, without the prior written consent of the Railway
options.B: Can sublet the work after merely informing the sectional staff
options.C: Can assign the contract to his creditors at his discretion
options.D: Is free to sublet the entire work to any other contractor

e: Under the GCC a contractor cannot sublet or assign the work or any part of it without the prior written consent of the Railway; unauthorised subletting is a breach of contract.

q: In the contract documents for a work, references to the 'Engineer' are to be understood as references to:

options.A: Any engineer employed by the contractor
options.B: The engineer who prepared the abstract estimate
options.C: The officer designated in the contract under whose supervision and direction the work is to be executed
options.D: The Chief Engineer of the Railway Board

e: Engineer in contract documents means the officer designated in the contract under whose supervision and direction the work is executed, not any engineer of the contractor or the estimate maker.

q: The successful tenderer receives the Letter of Acceptance but the formal agreement is yet to be signed, and he asks whether any contract exists at all. The correct position is that the Letter of Acceptance:

options.A: Is a mere formality with no legal effect
options.B: Communicates acceptance of his tender and brings the contract into existence, even before the formal agreement is executed
options.C: Entitles him to payment in advance for the whole work
options.D: Replaces the need for security deposit in all cases

e: The Letter of Acceptance communicates acceptance of the tender and brings a binding contract into existence at that point, even though the formal agreement is executed afterwards.

q: A change ordered in a contract is so extensive that the work as changed bears little resemblance to the work originally contracted for. Such a change, which alters the entire character of the contract, is described as:

options.A: A deviation
options.B: An extra item
options.D: Vitiation of the contract

e: A change so extensive that the changed work bears little resemblance to the original contract alters its entire character and is vitiation of the contract, beyond a normal deviation or extra item.

q: A contractor abandons a work midway and the contract is terminated for his default. The Railway gets the remaining work completed through another agency, and the extra cost so incurred is borne:

options.A: At the risk and cost of the defaulting contractor
options.B: Wholly by the Railways in every case
options.C: By the tender committee that awarded the original contract
options.D: By the new agency as a goodwill gesture

e: If a defaulting contractors work is completed through another agency after termination, the extra cost is recovered at the risk and cost of the defaulting contractor under the GCC.

q: Completion of a work is delayed because the Railway itself failed to hand over the site and to supply departmental materials in time. In such a case, extension of the completion period can be granted because the delay:

options.A: Is claimed by the contractor as a matter of right for any reason
options.B: Is entirely due to the neglect of the contractor
options.C: Is due to causes beyond the control of the contractor
options.D: Can never be granted under the General Conditions of Contract

e: Extension of time is justified where delay is due to causes beyond the contractors control, such as the Railways failure to hand over the site or supply departmental materials in time.

q: Soon after a completed work is handed over, defects appear in it during the maintenance period. Under the contract, these defects are required to be:

options.A: Repaired by the Railway at its own cost in all cases
options.B: Made good by the contractor at his own cost
options.C: Ignored until the work is taken up again for repairs
options.D: Charged to the contractor's security deposit without any notice to him

e: Defects appearing in the maintenance period must be made good by the contractor at his own cost under the GCC defect liability provisions; the Railway does not pay for rectifying his defective work.

q: Under an item-rate contract, the quantity of an item actually executed turns out to be more than the quantity shown in the schedule. The contractor is paid:

options.A: A lump sum for the whole work, irrespective of quantities
options.B: On a cost-plus basis
options.C: Only for the scheduled quantity, whatever was actually executed
options.D: For the actual quantities of each item executed, at the rates quoted by him for those items

e: In an item-rate contract, payment is for the actual quantities of each item executed, measured on site, at the rates quoted for those items - not a lump sum or only the scheduled quantities.

q: In a tender invited under the two-packet system, the financial packet of a tenderer is opened at the first stage itself along with his technical packet. This procedure is wrong because in this system:

options.A: The financial packets of only those tenderers whose technical packets are found acceptable are opened
options.B: The technical packet is opened only after the contract is awarded
options.C: Two separate contracts are awarded for one work
options.D: The financial packet is opened first and the technical packet later

e: In the two-packet system, financial packets are opened only for tenderers whose technical packets are found acceptable; opening a financial packet at the first stage defeats the system.

q: Rates received for a work are high and negotiations with tenderers become unavoidable. As a rule, such negotiations are to be held:

options.A: With all the tenderers one by one
options.B: With the highest tenderer
options.D: With the tenderer recommended by the executive

e: Where negotiations on works tenders are unavoidable, they are held as a rule only with the lowest tenderer, to bring his rates to a reasonable level, and not serially with all tenderers.

q: A tender committee is constituted to examine the tenders received for a work. Such a committee normally comprises:

options.A: Only the executive officer dealing with the work
options.B: The executive officer, the finance/accounts officer and an officer of another department
options.C: The General Manager and the Divisional Railway Manager
options.D: Representatives of the tenderers

e: A tender committee normally consists of the executive officer, a finance and accounts officer and an officer of another department, giving technical, financial and independent views on the tender.

q: In the deliberations of a tender committee, the finance member's distinctive contribution is to:

options.A: Prepare the tender documents
options.B: Execute the work after it is awarded
options.C: Inspect the work during its execution
options.D: See that the tender is financially sound, funds are available and financial propriety is observed

e: The finance member of a tender committee ensures the tender is financially sound, funds are available and financial propriety is observed, complementing the technical assessment of other members.

q: For a tender of low value, the accepting authority proposes to accept it on its own without placing it before a tender committee. This course, where permissible for tenders of low value, is known as:

options.A: Direct acceptance
options.B: Single tendering
options.D: Post-facto acceptance

e: Direct acceptance is the course for low-value tenders where the accepting authority may accept a tender on its own without a tender committee, as permitted by the tender rules.
